subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the shape of the BeCl2 molecule (gas phase)?
questions.explain: BeCl2 has 2 bonding pairs and no lone pairs on Be, giving a linear shape with a 180° bond angle.

questions.q: Which molecule is linear?
questions.explain: CO2 has two bonding regions (two double bonds) and no lone pairs on carbon, giving a linear shape with a 180° bond angle.

questions.q: Which statement about electronegativity across Period 3 (Na to Cl) is correct?
questions.explain: Electronegativity increases across a period because nuclear charge rises while atomic radius falls, so bonding electrons are attracted more strongly.

questions.q: What shape does the molecule SF4 adopt?
questions.explain: SF4 has 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair based on a trigonal bipyramid, giving a see-saw shape.

questions.q: Which type of bonding is present in solid magnesium?
questions.explain: Magnesium consists of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons, which is metallic bonding.

questions.q: What is the shape of a sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) molecule?
questions.explain: SF6 has 6 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving an octahedral shape with 90° bond angles.

questions.q: What is the bond angle between two equatorial bonds in a molecule of PF5?
questions.explain: PF5 is trigonal bipyramidal; the three equatorial bonds lie in a plane at 120° to each other.

questions.q: Why does iodine sublime easily at relatively low temperatures?
options: It is a simple molecular solid with weak van der Waals forces
questions.explain: Iodine forms a simple molecular lattice held together only by weak van der Waals forces, which are easily overcome.

questions.q: Why is ice less dense than liquid water?
options: Hydrogen bonds hold molecules in an open lattice
questions.explain: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in a regular open lattice with larger spaces, making it less dense than liquid water.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in the molecule XeF4 (square planar)?
questions.explain: XeF4 has 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (octahedral arrangement), giving a square planar shape with 90° F–Xe–F angles.

questions.q: Which molecule has a trigonal planar shape?
questions.explain: BF3 has 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, giving a trigonal planar shape; the others all have a lone pair.

questions.q: What is the shape of an ammonia (NH3) molecule?
questions.explain: NH3 has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape with a bond angle of about 107°.

questions.q: What is the predicted bond angle in a molecule of H2O?
questions.explain: Water has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs; lone-pair repulsion reduces the bond angle to about 104.5°.

questions.q: Which intermolecular force is responsible for the relatively high boiling point of HF compared with HCl?
questions.explain: HF forms hydrogen bonds because hydrogen is bonded to highly electronegative fluorine, raising its boiling point above HCl.

questions.q: Which of the following has the strongest intermolecular forces?
questions.explain: Butane (C4H10) has the most electrons and the largest surface area, so it has the strongest van der Waals forces of the four alkanes.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in a methane (CH4) molecule?
questions.explain: CH4 has 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around carbon, giving a tetrahedral shape with bond angles of 109.5°.

questions.q: Why does diamond have a very high melting point?
options: It is held by van der Waals forces
It is a giant covalent structure
questions.explain: Diamond is a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure in which every carbon is bonded to four others by strong covalent bonds requiring large energy to break.

questions.q: The ion CO3^2- has which shape?
questions.explain: The carbonate ion has 3 bonding regions around the central carbon and no lone pairs on it, giving a trigonal planar shape (120°).

questions.q: Which factor most strongly determines the strength of induced-dipole (van der Waals) forces between molecules?
questions.explain: The more electrons a molecule has, the larger the instantaneous and induced dipoles, so van der Waals forces increase with electron number.

questions.q: Why does water have a higher boiling point than hydrogen sulfide (H2S)?
questions.explain: Oxygen is sufficiently electronegative for water to form hydrogen bonds, which are stronger than the dipole-dipole forces in H2S, raising its boiling point.

questions.q: Which of these molecules is polar overall?
questions.explain: H2O is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel, giving a net dipole; the other three are symmetrical and non-polar.

questions.q: Which has a higher boiling point and why: butan-1-ol or pentane (similar Mr)?
questions.explain: Butan-1-ol has an O–H group allowing hydrogen bonding, which is stronger than the van der Waals forces in pentane, so it boils higher.

questions.q: Which bond is the most polar?
questions.explain: O–H has the largest electronegativity difference of the options, making it the most polar bond.

questions.q: Which species contains a dative (coordinate) covalent bond?
questions.explain: In NH4+ one N–H bond forms because the lone pair on nitrogen is donated to an H+ ion, making it a dative covalent bond.

questions.q: Why does NaCl have a high melting point?
options: Strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
questions.explain: NaCl is a giant ionic lattice with strong electrostatic forces between Na+ and Cl- ions that require much energy to overcome.

questions.q: Permanent dipole-dipole forces arise between molecules that:
questions.explain: Permanent dipole-dipole forces occur between molecules with a permanent net dipole, i.e. polar molecules.

questions.q: Why can graphite conduct electricity?
options: Each carbon has a delocalised electron
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon forms three covalent bonds, leaving one delocalised electron per atom that is free to move and carry charge.

questions.q: The molecule PCl3 has a bond angle closest to:
questions.explain: PCl3 has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair (like NH3), giving a trigonal pyramidal shape with a bond angle of about 107°.

questions.q: Which substance does NOT conduct electricity in any state because it has no charged particles free to move?
questions.explain: Diamond is a giant covalent structure with all four outer electrons of each carbon used in bonding, so there are no free charge carriers.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in a molecule of BF3?
questions.explain: BF3 has 3 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving a trigonal planar shape with 120° bond angles.
